subject: Staged advance commitment + escrow-style rate ceiling for renewal
messages:
From: Sofia Ramirez <sofia.ramirez@atlashealth.com>
To: Priya Natarajan <priya@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-08-09T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Renewal exposure / options to lock rate for 2028

Hi Priya,

We're starting to formalize our budget for 2028 and I'm concerned about the recent upward pressure on inference unit costs. We like Redwood's performance but we need a way to cap our rate before the formal renewal window opens.

Two quick asks:
- Do you offer any multi-year or advance-payment structures that effectively lock a ceiling on our per-token price?
- If so, how do you handle underspend / crediting if we don't hit the committed ramp?

We'd like to evaluate a proposal that reduces our exposure but doesn't require a full two-year prepay at once.

Sofia
Sofia Ramirez
Head of Procurement, AtlasHealth

Hi Sofia — thanks for the note and context. We can absolutely design a structure that reduces your rate exposure without forcing a full upfront multi-year payment. High level idea attached (term sheet):

Summary (attached: RDW_rate_lock_term_sheet_v1.pdf):
- Staged advance-commitment (18 months standard example): 3 tranches (6/6/6 months).
- Price ceiling: a guaranteed max per-token rate for the full 18 months.
- Holdback / escrow-style buffer: a portion (~10%) of each tranche is held as a reversible credit; if usage undershoots the ramp, we either refund the holdback pro-rata or convert to prepaid credits at the same ceiling price.
- Overage rules: usage above the prepay is billed at the ceiling price until tranche is exhausted, then at the standard metered rate thereafter.
- Ramp flexibility: we can accelerate tranche release if you provide early notice / usage forecast (useful for forecast management).

Why this helps Atlas: predictable unit economics (price ceiling) while providing a path to credit/refund if your actual usage falls short of the committed ramp. It balances cash flow and protects you from market rate increases.

Ask: can you share a 3-quarter expected usage profile (tokens/month) so I can run exact unit-price math? If agreeable, I can send a revision with an accelerated ramp option + a v2 term sheet that includes the exact pricing tiers.

Attached: RDW_rate_lock_term_sheet_v1.pdf, Atlas_SOW_draft.docx

Best,

Thanks Priya — this looks promising. A few clarifications before we run to finance:

1) Ramp schedule and credits: can you show an example where the second tranche can be accelerated at 30 days notice with reduced holdback? Atlas prefers shorter ramp-in periods if that lowers the net effective unit price earlier.
2) On the escrow-style holdback: what triggers a refund vs conversion to prepaid credits? Please confirm timing (quarterly reconciliation?) and whether refunds are net of any administrative fees.
3) Can you show both 12-month and 18-month variants side-by-side? Finance wants to see the delta in effective blended price and cashflow timing.

If you can share v2 with those two variants, we'll run it with procurement + finance next week.

Sofia

Hi Sofia — appreciate the quick feedback. Per our internal review we've prepared two clean variants and one accelerated-ramp addendum. Summary below and the updated term sheet attached (RDW_rate_lock_term_sheet_v2.pdf).

Variant A — 12 months (fast lock):
- Single upfront prepay covering 12 months at 8% discount off list;
- Price ceiling in contract: $0.0009 / token (ceiling applies to prepay and any overages during the 12 months);
- Holdback: 12% of prepay held as refundable credit; quarterly reconciliation, refund pro-rata if usage <= committed -10% over a reconciliation quarter (net of 1% admin fee).

Variant B — 18 months (staged):
- 3 tranches (6 / 6 / 6 months) prepaid at signing; blended effective discount ~12% off list (see model);
- Price ceiling: $0.00085 / token for the 18-month period;
- Holdback: 10% with quarterly reconciliation and conversion/refund rules as above.

Accelerated ramp addendum (optional):
- Atlas may trigger tranche 2 release with 30-day notice; when triggered, holdback for released tranche reduces by 50% (immediate cashflow relief) and the ceiling price for the released tranche is the Variant B ceiling.
- We retain the right to ask for short-term forecast to support accelerated release.

Other commercial notes:
- Deeper discount path: we can commit to an additional 4–6% off ceiling if Atlas agrees to a 24-month total commitment (mix of upfront + scheduled prepay).
- Contract mechanics: DocuSign link for the chosen variant included below.
